headline: Winless Estoril are still the favourites at home
summary: Estoril go into Sunday's game bottom of the Primeira Liga: 2 points from 8 matches, no win, and a coach change a week ago. A Bola reports the board sees this match as the real test for the in-house coach, and that forward Begraoui is a doubt with a muscle injury. Moreirense sit 12th but arrive after a 0-1 cup exit at AVS and concede 1.58 expected goals a game. Even so, the market across 10 bookmakers, margin removed, makes Estoril 50.6% favourites, rated about half a goal better on the handicap, with over 2.5 goals at 50.3%.
read: Bottom-of-the-table Estoril, winless in eight league games and with the club deciding this week on its coach, are still the market favourites at 50.6% at home to Moreirense. The goals line is close to a coin flip at 2.5, with both defences conceding more than they create and the last five meetings producing 18 goals.

facts.fact: Estoril go into the game bottom of the Primeira Liga with 2 points from 8 matches and no win.
facts.meaning: A home game against a side just above them is their clearest chance so far to change the direction of the season.

facts.fact: Estoril are the market favourites at 50.6%, more than double Moreirense's 23.5%.
facts.meaning: The market makes the bottom-placed side the more likely winner of this match.

facts.fact: Estoril confirmed the departure of coach Vasco Matos a week ago, with the team now run by an in-house coach.
facts.meaning: The side is being prepared through a change on the bench in the middle of a winless start.

facts.fact: A Bola reports Estoril's board is increasingly inclined to keep faith with its in-house coach, with the Moreirense match seen as the real test.
facts.meaning: This is the game the club itself is treating as the verdict on the coaching situation.

facts.fact: The handicap fair line is -0.54, with the main line set at -0.5.
facts.meaning: The market rates Estoril about half a goal better than Moreirense here.

facts.fact: Moreirense were knocked out of the Portuguese Cup 0-1 by AVS, Rodrigo Pinho scoring in the 3rd minute.
facts.meaning: They arrive with the league as their only route to a decent season, days after a cup elimination.

facts.fact: Moreirense have conceded an average of 1.58 xG per game this season, more than Estoril's 1.44.
facts.meaning: The away side's defence is the softest part of this match-up.

facts.fact: Estoril needed penalties to beat lower-league Salgueiros in the cup after a 1-1 draw, equalising in the 89th minute.
facts.meaning: Even their cup progress came without a convincing performance against weaker opposition.

sources.fact: Portuguese outlet A Bola reports that Estoril's board is increasingly inclined to keep faith with its in-house coach, with the Moreirense match seen as the real test.
OJogo reports that Estoril's SAD will decide by Wednesday whether Sérgio Raimundo is the permanent solution, with several names under consideration for the job.
A Bola reports that Moroccan forward Begraoui has picked up a muscle injury during the international break, raising concern for Estoril.
Estoril confirmed the departure of coach Vasco Matos, with Custódio and João Gião mentioned as possible successors.
Estoril needed penalties to beat lower-league Salgueiros in the Portuguese Cup after a 1-1 score at the end of extra time, having forced the extra period with a goal in the 89th minute.
Correio da Manhã describes Estoril as the last-placed team in the Primeira Liga going into the cup weekend.
Moreirense were eliminated from the Portuguese Cup, losing 1-0 to AVS SAD after Rodrigo Pinho scored the only goal in the 3rd minute.
Moreirense coach Vasco Botelho da Costa said after the cup exit that it may seem almost polemical but he has to be very satisfied with the performance.
